key_insight: QPipe uses an LLM-based multi-agent workflow to convert natural-language requirements into executable quantum applications for test optimization with high success rates.
engineering_relevance: The approach lowers the quantum-programming barrier for software engineering teams by automating workflow generation, code synthesis, execution, and verification.
method: Multi-agent pipeline: requirement parsing, formulation, code generation, review, execution, verification.
Targets real-world benchmark-driven test-optimization problems from natural-language requirements.
Produces traceable quantum-application workflows with iterative agent feedback.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on 20 NL requirements, QPipe achieved 100% average code compilation and 96.7% average application execution/final-result combination, with average cost of 260.1 seconds and 1.89M tokens per requirement.
watch_item: The system is token- and time-intensive, and its gains depend on preserving code-generation skill, task knowledge, review feedback, and multi-agent decomposition.
paper_title: Leveraging LLM-Based Agentic Systems to Generate Quantum Applications for Test Optimization
